# After the Hall of Fame: Pokémon Ruby NDS

What there is to do once you have entered the Hall of Fame: the event islands and their tickets, the roaming legendaries, gifts, new places and battles. Levels are the ones you meet in this game.

## Back home in Littleroot

After the credits you wake up in your room.

1. Go downstairs. Dad is home and gives you the **S.S. Ticket**.
2. Check the TV downstairs: a news bulletin about a blue Flying Pokémon. That is Latios, and it now roams Hoenn. (The news is only on the TV in your own house.)
3. Talk to Mom: a letter from the Lilycove ferry company, with the **Eon Ticket**.
4. Go outside. Prof. Birch is waiting by your door and takes you to his Lab, where your Pokédex becomes the **National Pokédex**. From then on Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres roam Hoenn too.

The S.S. Ticket lets you board the S.S. Tidal at Slateport's and Lilycove's harbors, to the Battle Tower island ([battles](#battles-after-the-hall-of-fame)).

## Roaming legendaries

| Pokémon | Level | Starts roaming |
|---|---|---|
| Latios | 44 | when you watch the news on the TV at home |
| Raikou | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Entei | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Suicune | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Articuno | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Zapdos | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Moltres | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |

- **Where:** Routes 110-111 and 117-134. Never in towns, caves or buildings.
- **Meeting one:** on the route where a roamer is, 1 in 4 wild battles in tall grass or on the water is the roamer (never when fishing). With several on the same route, it is one of them at random. A Repel keeps a roamer away only when your first Pokémon's level is higher than the roamer's.
- **They move:** each time you walk from one route or town into the next, every roamer moves to a route next to its own (now and then further away). When you fly, go through a door or load your game, they all jump to new routes at random.
- **In battle:** a roamer runs away as soon as it can. A move or Ability that traps it (such as Mean Look or Shadow Tag) stops it. The damage and status problems you gave it stay after it gets away.
- **Caught:** it stops roaming. **Knocked out:** it is gone until you next enter the Hall of Fame; then it roams again with full HP.
- **Tracking:** a roamer's AREA page in the Pokédex shows the route it is on right now (no area while it is not roaming).

## Event tickets and islands

| Ticket | Who gives it | Island | Pokémon |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eon Ticket | Mom, at home (after Dad gives you the S.S. Ticket) | Southern Island | Latias, Lv 55 |
| Old Sea Map | Capt. Stern, Slateport City harbor | Faraway Island | Mew, Lv 32 |
| Aurora Ticket | Prof. Cozmo, in his house in Fallarbor Town | Birth Island | Deoxys, Lv 32 |
| Mystic Ticket | Lanette, in her house on Route 114 | Navel Rock | Lugia and Ho-Oh, Lv 78 |

- Each ticket is given the first time you talk to that person after the Hall of Fame.
- Show the ticket at **Lilycove City's harbor** (the Slateport ferry doesn't sail to the islands). With several tickets you choose the island. Every island has a sailor who takes you back to Lilycove.
- While you hold the Eon Ticket and haven't been to Southern Island yet, the Lilycove ferry takes you there first.
- The first time you show the Old Sea Map, Mr. Briney sails you to Faraway Island himself.

### Southern Island

From the boat, walk into the middle of the island and on to the stone at its far end. Stand in front of it and read it. Latias flies down and battles you. **One chance only:** whatever happens in the battle, it doesn't come back and the ferry doesn't sail there again. Save before you read the stone.

### Faraway Island

When you go into the grassy middle of the island, Mew sees you and runs a few steps into the tall grass. Unlike Gen 3, it doesn't hide in the grass or move away as you walk: it stays in sight and wanders about a small patch of the tall grass on its own. Walk up next to it and talk to it to battle it. If it moves off, wait for it to stop near you.

### Birth Island

The triangle stands in the middle of the island top (in this game it looks like a white stone ball). Walk up from the dock and talk to it from below: it jumps to another spot. Each time it jumps, walk the shortest way to the side of it given here and talk to it again. Every step counts; turning on the spot does not.

| Jump | Talk to it from | Steps allowed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | above | 4 |
| 2 | below | 8 |
| 3 | above | 8 |
| 4 | right | 8 |
| 5 | left | 4 |
| 6 | above | 4 |
| 7 | right | 4 |
| 8 | left | 6 |
| 9 | above | 3 |
| 10 | below | 3 |

The 10th time you talk to it after a jump, it breaks and Deoxys appears. One step too many and it goes back to the middle: talk to it there from below and start again from jump 1. Leaving the island resets the puzzle.

Up to v19.0 the triangle always went back to the middle after its first jump, however you walked (a bug). The next update fixes it.

### Navel Rock

From the boat, go into the rock and on through the caves to the long tunnel, and walk to its far end. There the way forks:
- **Up:** the ladder on the left climbs through 4 small rooms to the summit. Walk up the narrow path: Ho-Oh flies down and battles you.
- **Down:** the ladder on the right goes down through 11 small rooms to the bottom, where Lugia waits. Talk to it to battle it.

### If you run, lose or knock one out (Mew, Deoxys, Lugia, Ho-Oh)

- **Caught:** it is gone from the island.
- **Ran away:** it is there again on your next visit (Deoxys: solve the triangle again).
- **You lose:** you black out, and it waits for your next visit.
- **Knocked out:** it flies away, and comes back after your next Hall of Fame.

## Gifts

- **Beldum** (Lv 5): the Poké Ball in Steven's house in Mossdeep City, after the Hall of Fame. You need room in your party.
- **Jirachi** (Lv 5): the scientist at the back of the Mossdeep Space Center (1F) gives it after the Hall of Fame. You need room in your party.
- **Celebi** (Lv 10): once you have the National Pokédex, it stands in the clearing in the north-east of Petalburg Woods, behind the girl who gives the Miracle Seed. Talk to it to battle it. If you run, it is back next time; if you knock it out, it comes back after your next Hall of Fame.
- **Enigma Berry**: Dad gives you one in Petalburg City Gym after the Hall of Fame (once; not while you already carry one).
- **Diploma**: catch all 200 Pokémon of the Hoenn Pokédex (Jirachi and Deoxys aren't needed) and talk to the game designer on the 2F of the Cove Lily Motel in Lilycove City. He and the rest of the game's staff are there after the Hall of Fame.

## New places

### Altering Cave

After the Hall of Fame a cave opens in the cliff on the north side of the water on Route 103 (Surf to it). Its wild Pokémon change by the day: Zubat until your first visit, then the next one in this list each new day you pass through Route 103 (after the last, back to the first).

| | Pokémon | Level |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Zubat | 6-16 |
| 2 | Mareep | 3-13 |
| 3 | Pineco | 19-31 |
| 4 | Houndour | 12-22 |
| 5 | Teddiursa | 6-16 |
| 6 | Aipom | 18-29 |
| 7 | Shuckle | 18-29 |
| 8 | Stantler | 18-29 |
| 9 | Smeargle | 18-29 |

### Mirage Island

Not tied to the Hall of Fame: the island shows on Route 130 (between Route 129 and Route 131) on days when the day's number matches a Pokémon in your party (Eggs too). That is 1 in 128 for each Pokémon each day, about 1 in 22 days with six. The number changes once a day. On the island: Wynaut (Lv 5-55) in the tall grass, and a Liechi Berry tree.

### Sky Pillar

After the Hall of Fame a rocky islet appears on Route 131 (west of Pacifidlog Town). Surf to it and go into the cave; at its far end you come out by the tower's door. Inside, take the stairs up floor by floor:
- **Cracked floors (2F and 4F):** walking onto a crack drops you to the floor below. Ride your Bicycle over them. Here any riding crosses them, slow or fast (in Gen 3 it took the Mach Bike at full speed).
- **4F:** the stairs up to 5F are in the top-left corner, and you can't ride there. Ride round to the narrow passage that runs just below that corner, get off the Bicycle, and walk onto one of the two cracks in the middle of the passage. You drop into a closed-off part of 3F; its stairs take you up into the corner, by the stairs to 5F.

At the top waits Rayquaza (Lv 78): talk to it. **One chance only:** whatever happens in the battle, it doesn't come back. Save before you talk to it.

### The Sealed Chamber

The three Regi chambers open together, from the Sealed Chamber under the sea of Route 134. Braille in this game is shown as the plain text it spells.

1. On Route 134, Surf to the patch of dark deep water (the current stops there) and Dive ([field moves](tms-and-hms.md#field-moves-without-hms)).
2. Underwater, swim south into the opening below you, then follow the trench down to its far end. Stand just below the braille there ("Go up here.") and press A to surface. (In Gen 3 it was B. Surfacing anywhere else brings you back up on Route 134.)
3. You come up in the Sealed Chamber. Walk to the braille in the middle of the top wall ("Dig here.") and step onto the floor right in front of it with a Pokémon in your party that knows Dig: it digs through the wall for you. It must be a Pokémon that knows Dig (the TM in your Bag is not enough; no badge is needed).
4. Go through. Put Relicanth first and Wailord last in your party (the last Pokémon you carry, however many you have), then read the braille on the far wall ("First comes Relicanth. Last comes Wailord."). The room shakes: the three chambers are open.

### The three Regi chambers

Each is a small cave with braille on the back wall of its first room. Stand in front of the braille and read it, then do what it says: the wall behind it opens. Go through and talk to the Regi. When a field move is needed, you don't choose it from the menu: step onto the right spot and it is used for you, as long as you could use it there ([field moves](tms-and-hms.md#field-moves-without-hms): the badge, then a Pokémon that knows the move or its TM or HM in your Bag).

- **Desert Ruins (Route 111), Regirock.** The braille: "Right, right, down, down. Then, use Strength." Strength is used when you step onto the spot 2 steps right and 2 steps down from the one in front of the braille. (Heat Badge; HM04 Strength.)
- **Island Cave (Route 105), Regice.** The braille: "Stop and wait. Wait for time to pass twice." Read it and then just wait: the message stays up for about 2 minutes, then the wall opens. Here pressing a button doesn't spoil the wait (in Gen 3 it did).
- **Ancient Tomb (Route 120), Registeel.** The braille: "With new time, hope and love, aim to the sky in the middle." Fly is used when you step onto the middle of the room, 4 steps straight down from the spot in front of the braille. You cross it when you walk straight up from the entrance. (Feather Badge; HM02 Fly.)

## Battles after the Hall of Fame

- **The Pokémon League** can be challenged again. The Elite Four and the Champion keep their teams.
- **Wally** waits in Victory Road 1F for a battle (Lv 48-53; his team is on the [trainers page](trainers-ruby.md#wally)).
- **The Battle Tower island**: take the S.S. Tidal from Slateport or Lilycove with the S.S. Ticket.

### Battle Tower

- Two rooms: **Lv. 50** (your Pokémon must be level 50 or lower; the opponents are level 50) and **Lv. 100** (any level; the opponents are level 100). Your Pokémon keep their own levels.
- Three Pokémon, no Eggs, no species twice and no held item twice. Not allowed: Mewtwo, Mew, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Celebi, Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza, Jirachi and Deoxys.
- A challenge is seven battles in a row; your Pokémon are healed between battles. You can save and quit between battles and go on later.
- Prize for each challenge won: one of HP Up, Protein, Iron, Calcium, Carbos or Zinc (at random) for your first 6 challenges in a row, then one of BrightPowder, White Herb, Quick Claw, Leftovers, Mental Herb, King's Rock, Focus Band, Scope Lens or Choice Band.
- When a challenge ends with more than 55 wins in a row, the three Pokémon get the Winning Ribbon (Lv. 50) or the Victory Ribbon (Lv. 100).
- A man in the lobby awards the Silver Shield at a best streak of 50 and the Gold Shield at 100: decorations for your Secret Base.

### Pokémon World Tournament (PWT)

The second building on the island is Black 2's PWT. The left desk offers the Driftveil, Rental and Mix tournaments (Download needs Nintendo's closed online service). The right desk offers the Unova Leaders and Hoenn Leaders tournaments, and more as you win them, as in Black 2 (Kanto, Johto and Sinnoh Leaders after the Unova Leaders, then World Leaders and Champions). Battle Points won there are spent at the lobby's counters.

Gym Leader and trainer rematches are in Pokémon Emerald NDS only.
